Python C64/6502 PRG disassembler with entry-point controls and address map comments. Inspected repository README and source/tree where relevant.
D64 BoozeLoader/ByteBoozer trackmo extraction and decrunching; experimental BASIC/disassembly routines. Inspected repository README and source/tree where relevant.
Curated listings and reference material, without a distinct buildable analysis project.
GitHub fork metadata identifies mist64/final_cartridge parent.
Repository tree contains only an item-list Markdown file.
README index points to separately catalogued game repositories.

Reconstructs v1.20 using Turbo C 2.0 and TASM 1.0. Author reports 96.30% identical load-image bytes after excluding EXE headers/relocations; remaining mismatch includes uninitialized data, so do not mark byte-exact.

Author reports the reconstructed executable is byte-for-byte identical for the documented LZEXE shareware and registered builds. Separate from the same author's modern RigelEngine port; shares historical engine lineage with Cosmore.

Reconstructs v451.03 game C code and most related executables with a functionally equivalent loader. C routines can match original instructions when compiled with Microsoft C 5.1, but executable layout differences and remaining assembly mean no whole-binary exactness claim. Modern port is a separate derivative.

Author reports release builds reproduce original DOS binaries and all three SAR archives bit for bit via build_masm.py --verify; the C/WebAssembly port is playable to the ending. Separate from awkto's independent Zeliard study and SDL port.

Version 1.6 debug symbols informed an author-reported Ghidra/AI decompilation; Borland C++ 3.x build produces PACWARS.EXE, with DOSBox IPX launch scripts. No binary identity or complete gameplay parity established.

The original branch preserves per-function offsets into the v1.1 DOS binary; main has an SDL2 C/C++ port with touch controls and changes. Do not treat the modern executable as a byte-exact DOS reassembly.

Assembly files patch portions of the original DOS executable via incbin; fixes include smooth scrolling, copy-protection bypass, input and sound changes. This is not a full game disassembly or reconstructed source tree.
README documents stripping a 16-bit DOS extender around a 32-bit game and the gog/ tree contains a large rayman_disasm.S listing. Research output is an analysis/disassembly, not a working port.

Partial executable disassembly and tools for RLE, EGA images and castle layouts; extractors recover some volumes and first six castles. Runnable refers to the analysis extractors, not a playable game reconstruction.
Python save decoder/editor and tile decoder derived by modifying and inspecting game data. Author describes map decoding as unfinished and not published; there is no reconstructed gameplay source.

README calls a full Ghidra-derived reimplementation a goal; current UTILS contain music player/converter, resource extractor and graphics format work. Do not report a completed decompilation or playable port.
Viewer/editor for original DAT resources, maps, sprites, images, music, sound, text and triggers. Credits srtuss for the map format and joint research; game executable remains original.

Port of DOS Prince of Persia 1.0 based on the author's separately published IDA disassembly, with later-version features and modern extensions. The Apple II original source is cited as supporting evidence, not the DOS code being catalogued.

Buildable native Carmageddon reimplementation that replaces original assembly with C function by function. Historical Watcom symbols exist but README says they do not match released code positions. Completeness and playable parity remain unverified.

Unofficial modern engine using original game data; README states episode 1 is playable while episodes 2/3, saving and some audio/UI behavior remain incomplete. CPU of original binary not independently established.

From-scratch port of the 1995 DOS shooter; README reports all seven levels and ending playable using original disc image. Documents original programmer's format notes, manual Ghidra analysis, later AI-assisted implementation; modern code is not source-level decompilation.
Primary README explicitly documents 32-bit x86, WebAssembly, ARM Cortex-A7 and TMS320C6745 builds and links Tube64 as its 64-bit successor.

Separate from Duke2Reconstructed: modern C++ engine informed by original DOS disassembly; reads original game data and supports all four episodes. README directs readers to the same author's byte-exact reconstruction for historically faithful DOS code.

Independent repository with SAR/resource tools, original-binary disassembly scripts, documented town/fight systems, SDL port and author-described playthrough. CI tests without game files; parity/playthrough checks need original files. Separate from nolanvenhola's bit-perfect MASM reconstruction.

Earlier independent SCI Companion project corpus with title-specific game.ini, decompiled script source and occasional gameplay fixes; King's Quest I README reports completion testing but a moveButterfly caveat. Overlaps subjects with sluicebox/sci-scripts yet differs in versions, tooling history and human edits; no blanket script-build claim.
Original repository documents a parser, version detection and independent comparison against historical GFA editor output; distinct from tracked gfalist.
Primary README documents distinct reverse-direction format encoder and verification against real GFA-BASIC tools.

Implemented Commodore/NES Ghidra loaders, bundled SNES SPC700/65C816 language variants and bank-aware analysis; current 65C816 work quarantines one named bad oracle vector behind regression tripwires rather than treating it as a language failure.
Reviewed as one coherent multi-system music-sequence archaeology/extraction project; platform directories share one root purpose and do not warrant artificial subproject records.
Tool's README and CLI show concrete CPC-oriented Z80 reverse-engineering capabilities and runnable script.
Cycle-backend game-mod documentation and tests reviewed after the widescreen/mod merge: hooks, isolated calls, save-state records, presented width and custom rendering are opt-in and bounded.
Title-specific README documents native recompilation of verified US ROM and limited playable starting-area functionality.
Primary README documents three distinct game disassembly-to-JavaScript ports and per-frame emulator comparisons within one shared project.

Independent MEGA65/C64 research article on original Crossroads machine-code analysis; links to a renamed Crossroads II disassembly already tracked under MarkRdgOx. Follow original Crossroads research for further substantive artifacts.
Independent Amiga debugger reconstruction using disassembled ARIV/Action Replay material and new features; discovered via broad README search.

Buildable Merlin32/ca65 adaptation of the Brutal Deluxe VisiCalc disassembly. Recovers two regions left undecoded in the earlier listing, corrects code/data boundaries, and generates a DOS 3.3 disk image. README says source-only corrections retain byte-identical binaries; this is credited follow-on analysis, not the original disassembly. Whole-program match against the source binary is not claimed.

Annotated 1983 T&E SOFT ROM assembles to the original verbatim. Enhanced and Enhanced+ variants change graphics, sound, rooms and difficulty; their outputs should not be described as byte-identical to the original. README states the enhanced RAM start is $E000 and its RAM requirement is 8 KB, but does not establish the original ROM's minimum.

Annotated disassembly of Konami's RC727 game. Sjasm can assemble either ROM version using VERSION2; version 2 contains bug fixes. The source file documents the original/version differences; the README does not claim byte-identical builds.

Disassembled BIRDSK2 with WFDis/Beebdis and reassembled it with BeebAsm. Diagnoses and repairs graphical corruption after level 13 and a crash at level 23; includes playable binary, disk image and emulator save states. Later comments incorporate labels from the author's original sources.

Modular Python 3.11+ framework for recovering DOS games and developing native source ports. Combines static facts, original-executable oracle runs, deterministic replays and partial generated or authored implementations; it is a framework, not a completed port of a specific game or a universal decompiler.

Reconstructed C engine for the 1992 DOS English release, with format decoders and documentation. Two Open Watcom targets: structure-faithful BUMPY.EXE is link-only and byte-compared but not run; BUMPYP.EXE adds a host layer and plays in DOSBox with user-supplied game files. Author explicitly describes Claude-led work; no byte-identical final build claim.

Reconstructs the 1993 game from DOS binaries and reports full byte matches for both 1.00 floppy and 1.02 CD-ROM releases. Build recreates a Borland/TASM toolchain and requires user-supplied original game files for play; project also includes a browser-based asset viewer. The author says source cleanup and documentation remain ongoing.

Independent, heavily annotated disassembly of K240's play executable, reassembled with vasm as a drop-in replacement for the original game files. Repairs ship, fleet, economy and UI bugs and credits tetracorp's separate K240 analysis for assistance. The patched output is deliberately different from the original, so no original byte-match is asserted.

Analyzes a user-supplied Amiga WHDLoad install, its BOND-compressed overlays and three partially decoded 68000 modules that reassemble byte-for-byte. A playable Musashi/OCS host still executes original game code; a separate native no-Musashi translation has progressed into live combat but is not a finished whole-game recompilation. Distinct from the tracked Battle Squadron music replayer.

Native C reimplementation of the original Amiga game's gameplay and renderer, using the historical 68000 assembly source as reference and preserving Amiga data formats. SDL2 desktop and Emscripten builds are documented. This is source-derived porting, not a disassembly of an Amiga binary; no Amiga executable is run by the port.

Reverse engineers the packed Stage swaptro extracted from Sanity's Velveteen 18 disk, documents its load address and memory map, and provides buildable 68000 source plus several patch-based visual/music variants. README includes a Makefile workflow for applying patches, assembling and making a floppy; game playability is not applicable to a demo.

Web and Linux workbench for Amiga floppy, hard-drive, archive and ROM images. Current release documents RDB partition work, Amiga filesystems, resident modules, Hunk analysis, annotated 68k disassembly and exact-hash guarded patches. It is host-side tooling, not software running on an Amiga; some historical-media and emulator-dependent tasks require user-supplied inputs.

Complete, named 68000 source for Reservoir Gods' Atari ST Chu Chu Rocket 1.18 LITE. Default build reproduces CHUCHU.TOS and CHUCHU.LNK byte-identically; optional Reforged optimizations and fixes deliberately differ. README reports tests in Hatari and on a real Mega STe and explicitly credits Claude assistance. This is distinct from the original game's development source.

Builds a new loader, version-guarded patches for the Ator-cracked ST game, a simultaneous third-player mode and a joystick test utility. Fixes TOS 2.06/STE/Mega STE compatibility and requires the user's exact original input file; the game itself is not distributed or built by CI. Patched output is not an original byte-match.

Web and Linux workbench for Atari ST through Falcon floppy, hard-drive, archive and ROM images. Current release documents GEMDOS editing, AHDI/ICD partitions, STX protection reports, flux containers and 68000 analysis. It is host-side tooling, not a native Atari ST application; the Amiga File Forge sibling handles a different platform and formats.
Game-specific Moonstone Amiga recovery and Windows adaptation with embedded 68000 core, custom OCS and game-specific hooks
Original Go parser/converter for AmigaBASIC tokenized program files, with name and keyword recovery
Python decompiler for tokenized Amiga BASIC files with extended keyword, numeric and name-table decoding
Command-line disassemblers and reusable decoders for Atari TOS 68000 executables and Falcon DSP files
C89 implementation of GFA BASIC 3.5 interpreter with Atari ST PRG build and host runtime
Populous fork with partial game-specific C translation and SDL2 Amiga hardware compatibility layer; architecture audit needed
Independent annotated Acorn ROM disassemblies with reassembly verification
Amiga Copper-list binary inspection tool with C source and sample output
Graduate CP/M ROM disassembly; AMSDOS listing separately identified as copied predecessor work
BBC Micro Nevryon disassembly and disk/asset analysis
BBC Micro Repton 2 disassembly and reassembly scripts
Author-released ASM-One sources for multiple historical Abyss Amiga demos and music discs; some contributions are partial, so the collection is not represented as full source for every production.

Recovered Tim and Geoff Follin period music and driver source from Tatung Einstein floppies. Author reverse-engineered a 6502 detokenizer and began modern Z80 assembler builds for AY music examples; this is source recovery, not a game disassembly.
Python extraction and documented analysis of original game map, charset, tile and sprite data. Scope is game data; no disassembly or playable reconstruction is claimed.

Disassembled C64 tuning and receiver programs from the 1985 Light Fantastic televised software-transmission experiment and documented receiver behaviour; the author says the recovered receiver appears to lack the storage part.
VICE save states and research notes documenting experimental reverse engineering of C64 demo effects; the README explicitly says the work is still limited in scope.

LangGraph-based research workbench accepts a 64 KB C64 memory dump and question, combines static Capstone disassembly with optional VICE MCP introspection and maintains an evidence-backed knowledge base. Separate from the tracked C64RE/TRX64 projects.
Fully annotated MSX2 Metal Gear disassembly with Sjasm ROM builds for the Japanese and English releases.
Manually annotated Arkanoid MSX disassembly with a documented z80asm rebuild and reference SHA-1.
PC-98 visual-novel engine research, executable disassemblies and format tools covering several engines and games.
Current C++ MES bytecode compiler/decompiler and GP4/GPC/GPA image round-trip tooling for PC-98 visual-novel engines.
Racket predecessor implementation explicitly credited by lime-juice; retained as lineage rather than a duplicate catalogue record.
Long-running bit-perfect source reconstruction of the first five Touhou PC-98 games.
Neko Project II fork with PC-98 binary-debugging features built for Touhou translation and ReC98 work.
OCR and proofreading restoration of Atari's paper OS-B source listing with a ca65 conversion and ROM comparison checks.
Sparse but substantive annotated 6502 disassembly of Bruce Lee for Atari 8-bit computers.

Reviewed all eight canonical submodule roots. Five titled homebrew games were promoted; the book, lesson-code and small-demo collections were classified as discovery nodes rather than single project records.
Redistributed MSX dumping, backup, repair and development tool bundle retained as an ecosystem discovery node.
Reusable Rust 68000 CPU core with tested instruction disassembly and assembly; not a complete Amiga or Atari ST emulator.
F# ST emulator boots TOS 1.00 to GEM, runs disk programs and Super Sprint, checks 68000 instruction vectors, and includes ROM/program control-flow investigations.
Port of uae4all-psp to the SF2000/GB300 multicore framework, with ADF loading and working save states; distinct from original UAE and WinUAE.
Maintained stable UAE 0.8.29 core focused on old A500 games and demos; docs/README describes the former master copy and its relationship to WinUAE/E-UAE.
General-purpose multi-platform reversing framework; the README gives no distinct legacy-platform project or extension to track here.
6502 core and system emulators with source/disassembly VS Code debugger, Lua scripting and TCP remote control; its README warns that system accuracy is incomplete.
Curated index of JavaScript emulators; useful for targeted discovery, but not an authored emulator itself.
Large curated game-format/resource index; useful as a source, not a standalone analysis tool.
Traces reachable code in ROM/memory images, supports driver-script annotations and pluggable CPU/environment/assembler renderers including BeebAsm/64tass output.
Annotated KEYPAD and JOYSTIK driver/loader disassemblies recreate the original files byte-for-byte, including BASIC tokenization and rotated payload encoding.
Amiga development and internals reference, rather than an implemented retro software or analysis tool.
Consumer PlayStation emulation port for SF2000/GB300; no project-specific recovery or source-debugging function established.
Structured low-level language/compiler for 6502-family computers and 68000, with experimental Amiga 500/1200 targets; README says the m68k targets are not yet production-ready.
Atari 2600 emulator with developer debugger, mapper and coprocessor support, and development-focused Supercharger/tape handling.
Broad security/reverse-engineering link compilation dominated by modern platforms, not a distinct retro-development project.
General debugging-story link index; its incidental C64 link is not an authored retro software project.
Open-source Game Boy/Color/Super Game Boy emulator with integrated debugger and MCP server for automated inspection and testing.
ColecoVision and ADAM emulator with integrated debugger and MCP server; an independent target within the Gear family.
PC Engine/TurboGrafx/SuperGrafx and CD-ROM emulator with integrated debugger and MCP server.
Master System/Game Gear/SG-1000 emulator with integrated debugger and MCP server.
Reverse-engineered 1989 C64 game with cc65 assembly and BASIC components; README says rebuilt output can match the original binary.
Original browser-based incremental game with a C64 emulator, without documented legacy-software reconstruction or a reusable retro-development tool.
Open-source Commander X16 hardware emulator with VERA, storage and ROM support, useful for reproducible X16 development.
2026 Acorn Electron port of the BBC Micro game; distributed as playable UEF/SSD images requiring 48K. Repository does not publish port source.
Small original binary-only visual simulation inspired by a modern web toy; no original-software archaeology or substantial conversion established.
2026 Acorn Electron 48K fan conversion of the ZX Spectrum game, distributed as playable UEF/SSD images; no port source is published here.
Consolidated CLI/API for managing annotated 6502 disassemblies across versions, including round-trip verification with BeebAsm; can use Dasmos or py8dis drivers.
Amiga ProTracker 2 continuation based on re-sourcing/disassembly of ProTracker 2.3D; source modifies playback and sample handling, with downloadable executable and bootable ADF.
QBasic Gorillas recreated in C64 BASIC with changed graphics/sound; repository includes authored BASIC source, not a disassembly of the DOS binary.
Instructions for running an older third-party Windows cartridge creator in a VM; no authored cartridge/tool reconstruction in this repository.
CPC/Plus and GX4000 emulator with sub-cycle hardware models, flux-image decoding, an integrated debugger and TCP/headless IPC for scripted analysis; no claim of independent feature verification.

Amstrad CPC firmware adapted to RC2014 with serial keyboard/text I/O and changed firmware routines; compatible BASIC can run through the firmware jump blocks. README describes a temporary pageable-ROM release.

Restored and documented Ian Bell/David Braben original C64 source discs, with BeebAsm build tooling and reference binaries. README shows matching compiled outputs for documented variants; original source provenance is explicit, not a disassembly-derived reconstruction.
KiCad hardware pinout symbols for CPC ICs; no software analysis or developer tool is implemented here.
Arduino-ready Z80 single-instruction disassembler handles incomplete opcode streams; the README explicitly excludes a hardware connection, full-program control-flow analysis and label generation.
Game-specific C64 compatibility engine for recent Covert Bitops titles; assess its execution path and relationship to the games before a catalogue record.
Web/C++ port of the same game-specific engine; assess alongside the Unity implementation rather than counting as a separate game reconstruction.

JavaScript reimplementation derived from CPC DSK and Z80 analysis; documents the original cooperative bytecode VM and includes disasm.c, bytecode listings and assembly. Do not infer byte-exact source.
Hand-redrawn Amiga font assets; the README expressly says the font file format was not reverse engineered.

Portable C recreation of the 1986 ST text-to-speech synthesizer, with original binary disassemblies and documented code-lineage comparison; claims sample-for-sample output, not original source or binary equality.
SNDH/PSG player with 68000 emulation, tracing and reachability-guided SNDH disassembly; output can be edited and reassembled to alter metadata or code.
Amiga device-driver example/template with optional generated objdump output; no legacy-software recovery or standalone analysis tool.

The hardware repository includes authored Amiga RTG driver source under drivers/gfx; README describes reverse-engineering the Picasso96 driver interface to get Workbench running. Scope is the driver, not a claim that the graphics-card hardware is software archaeology.
Action Replay III hardware schematic reproduction, GAL programming files and ROM binaries; no published debugger source reconstruction.
Amiga assembly tutorials and a mixed link list; useful for discovering upstream tools and analyses, not a single recovery project.
VS Code extension integrating VASM/VLINK, FS-UAE/WinUAE run/debug and Capstone disassembly for stack selection and source-less debugging.
Reverse-engineered third-party Amiga HD floppy-drive adapter hardware and PAL logic; no floppy software or media-analysis tool.

Includes ACME-assemblable C64 KERNAL source and release ROMs for C64/1541; README distinguishes the untouched original v1 ROM release. No evidence here of published 1541 source or binary-exact reproduction.

Original MiST Atari ST/STE FPGA core models GLUE/MMU from recovered schematics and shifter from reverse engineering; supports TOS and disk images. MiSTer-devel/AtariST_MiSTer adapts the core to distinct MiSTer board integration.

Board-specific adaptation of gyurco/MiSTery with MiSTer emu top-level, video and peripheral integration. README credits the upstream core, while AtariST.sv names and implements the MiSTer port; distinguish integration work from original chip reverse engineering.
Original CPC BASIC/C homebrew game and sprite-design examples; cited BASIC disassembly is a third-party reference, not project-specific archaeology.
Original browser-based JavaScript compiler and CPC runtime, still receiving bug fixes. README points to CPCBasicTS as a separately maintained TypeScript continuation with new features.
TypeScript continuation based on benchmarko/CPCBasic 0.9.20, with independently developed features including tokenized BASIC and DSK/ZIP import; the original JavaScript codebase has its own record.
Python tools list visible/hidden ROM commands, dump strings with optional XOR decoding and patch Graduate CP/M accessory ROM personal data; analysis is tied to real CPC ROM structures.
Cross-development collection includes AMSDOS header viewer, DSK sector tooling, screenshot/media converters and Caprice 32-derived emulator; README describes unfinished components separately.

The Documentation/VDP Emulator directory supplies original/patched Vampire Killer Z80 listings and diffs explaining Aleste game BIOS/VDP adaptation; surrounding repository is a broader Aleste hardware/software archive. Build and current playability not established.

Original Angus Duggan source discs, documented and modernized for BeebAsm; README compares built outputs with reference binaries and reports matching released variants, without calling this a disassembly.

Restored and documented Ian Bell/David Braben source discs for BBC Micro with 6502 Second Processor, with variant builds and reference-binary checksum checks; original source, not binary-derived disassembly.
Mixed archive of period CPC sources, tools and commercial work; components need individual attribution and scope before promotion.
Go emulator with Spectrum/CPC/MSX/NES and arcade modes, debugger/breakpoint flags and tests. README labels systems as incomplete (e.g. CPC 80%), so do not imply complete fidelity.
Authored Python scripts edit the Jose Leandro 512K cartridge ROM menu and insert game ROMs at known offsets; author disclaims authorship of original ROM and cartridge.
Port of the author’s new game to AmigaOS using offline sprite baking; no historical-game binary research or reusable analysis tool.
Native port of available OpenTTD 1.0.5 source to AmigaOS with substantial new platform drivers; no recovery of historical binaries established.

Original PRG self-extractor executed with Py65; recovered C64 code, graphics and timing informed a native Z80 Spectrum 48K TAP. RE notes explicitly reject cycle-perfect equality and document changed display and controls.; Separate JavaScript/canvas reimplementation of this repository’s native Spectrum port. README explicitly says there is no Z80 emulator or embedded binary and explains timing differences; do not equate it with a C64 direct port.
Original Z80 breadboard computer tutorial and schematics; no legacy-software reconstruction or separate analysis tool.
Replacement CPC keyboard PCB designs and matrix wiring; hardware only.
Hypothetical new 6502 CPC-like computer based on inspiration from a prototype PCB, not a reconstruction of its software.
CPC-compatible modular hardware and small test ROM/assembly snippets; no separately implemented CPC software archaeology project.
Untested HAL/PAL replacement hardware design and behavior tests; no developer software or recovered firmware.
Early work-in-progress Pascal-like cross compiler targeting Z80, with compiler, emulator and IDE source; README does not establish production use.
Hyperlinked CPC firmware manual, useful to verify firmware/jumpblock semantics but not an implemented analysis tool.
Original Z80 LCD circuit and test code; hardware tutorial outside legacy software/tooling scope.
Reusable 50 Hz scrolling engine and developer tools, sprite cache/multiplexer, loaders and example disk/cartridge builds; not a reconstruction of Steel Ranger or MW ULTRA.
Author website and downloadable C64 tool/game archive; useful as a provenance source, not an independent single software project.
Original C64 game source; retain to audit the specific games actually run by OldschoolEngine 2, not a binary reconstruction.
Original low-raster-time C64 music player with GoatTracker 2 converter and source; v2 is separately maintained and changes effects and hard restart behavior.
New player implementation retains lineage with cadaver/miniplayer but adds ADSR/waveform commands and changes hard restart and memory layout; README documents speed and NTSC tradeoffs.
Original Metal Warrior 4 C64 game source, useful context for the author’s game-specific emulator lineage.
Emulates 6502 instructions to dump SID register activity; README version history documents illegal opcode, multispeed and CPU-cycle profiling support.
Configurable recursive SID file scanner matches wildcard/skip-byte patterns against playroutine signatures; identifies provenance candidates rather than proving authorship.
Original source of the C64 Steel Ranger demo; useful for the OldschoolEngine 2 audit, not itself reverse engineering.
Acorn Electron binary-only consumer CHIP-8 emulator without documented developer debugger, analysis or source recovery capabilities.

Original developers captured a Spectrum snapshot, profiled executed regions and produced editable Z80 assembly; README says intro and second stage are absent and source is not yet ready for complete reassembly. CPC release is historical context only.

Authored browser game logic and scenes using assets from the CPC version and explicitly crediting Giner/Pazos disassembly/SDL work; README calls it playable with known bugs. Distinct Web implementation, not an independently recovered CPC disassembly.
VS Code C64 development suite with toolchain, resource compilers, VICE debugging, embedded 6502 emulation and disassembly; Atari ST search origin was incidental.

Retargetable assembler that also generates a disassembler and examples/tests from instruction definitions; README marks many architectures partial and explicitly supports usable 6502 and Game Boy programs.
Translates C64 BASIC and KERNAL behavior from documented disassemblies to the DCPU-16 fantasy CPU, with working command subset and PETSCII/display adaptation; not an original 6502 source archive.
Adapts the 1984 C64 SMON monitor to a Ben Eater style 6502 machine with serial IO and HEX loading; published assembly and ROM, with explicit removed C64 disk/printer features.
Traces 6502 code into IR and emits .NET MSIL for execution, with C64 and NES example emulators; JIT handles self-modifying code via invalidation. Distinct from highbyte/dotnet-6502 system emulator.
Annotated assembly adapts BBC BASIC to a Ben Eater-style 6502 ROM with serial I/O. Credits annotated BBC BASIC ROM disassemblies; README calls it alpha and warns LCD/keyboard drivers are broken.
Historical Windows/OS/2 Kermit terminal and file-transfer application source; this candidate documents an application continuation without a specific recovery or retro development tool contribution.
MAME front end with a custom Apple II/Macintosh-focused MAME build and Uthernet II support; a system emulator rather than a disassembly.
Maintained Jaguar and Jaguar CD libretro emulator. Repository documents processor/peripheral models and hardware-behavior test suite; no claim of new reverse engineering of a particular game.
General file-system-independent archive/recovery container; no historical computer software or platform-specific analysis in the project scope.
Curated website of retro reverse-engineering articles, file formats and source/code links. Retain as a discovery source for targeted follow-up, not as one project for every outbound link.
Beta reimplementation of WarpOS powerpc.library API/ABI for PowerPC PCI accelerators on Amiga. The repository is described as a CVS mirror; preserve that provenance.
Amiga-specific ISO C runtime and headers written from scratch to support GCC-based Amiga development. No claim that it was recovered from a binary.
HID to Amiga/Atari input adapter hardware and firmware; no independent historical-software recovery or developer-analysis tool evidenced.
GPL AmiTCP/IP 3.0b2 fork with separately implemented Roadshow-compatible bsdsocket.library extensions based on the published SDK ABI. Explicitly does not contain or disassemble Roadshow code.

Python MCP server and AmigaOS C daemon for remote shell, files, screenshots, ARexx and GUI interaction. README states AmigaOS 2.04 and bare 68000 for agent; AI integration is described, not an assertion about code authorship.
Full GEOS KERNAL 2.0 disassembly, reorganized and optimized for customization. README documents ACME/make assembly; altered sources are not asserted byte-identical to the original.
Game engine reimplementation based on reversing the original Windows executable; original Bermuda Syndrome game data is required.
Fade to Black engine reimplementation that loads original PC retail/demo data. README lists rendering and game options; original files are required.
Yaga-engine wrapper for two Humongous Entertainment games, using original .exe and .he/.da2 data. README flags missing lipsync; assess exact reverse-engineering lineage separately.
Disassembles NES ROM and rewrites hardware I/O to 65C816 routines before assembling a SNES ROM. Indirect jump targets require runtime observation and manual inclusion; compatibility is limited.
Open silicon pin-compatible Z80 CPU replacement with tapeout and PCB validation; hardware recreation outside the software catalogue.
Research and reproducible cycle/memory comparisons of more than 120 credited 6502 multiplication routines; useful developer reference, not a game disassembly.
Distinct Basilisk II libretro port for SF2000/GB300, emulating classic Macintosh and requiring a ROM and HFS disk image. No special debugging capability claimed.
Original modern Electron/BBC game distributed as tape/disk and executable images; no source-recovery or development-tool output in this release repository.
Original modern Electron/BBC game distributed as tape/disk and executable images; no source-recovery or development-tool output in this release repository.
Original modern Electron/BBC game release images and instructions, without a demonstrated software archaeology or tooling component.
Electron/BBC adaptation distributed as playable tape/disk images only; no distinct analysed-source or developer-tool artifact.
Electron Lode Runner game release images and play/edit instructions; no evidenced recovered source or development tooling here.
Distributed machine/emulator detection routine for Electron timing-sensitive code, with documented X-register IDs and an authored BeebAsm example. Core is distributed as disk/tape image.
Electron game release derived from a credited BBC Micro version; this release repository contains game images, not the predecessor analysis or source.
Packaged VS Code syntax-highlighting extension for max65 6502/65C02 assembly. Source is not asserted available in this release repository.
Playable enhanced Electron Meteors image; source/provenance for reverse engineering is not established by this release-only repository.
Python is the title of an original Electron/BBC game here (written in e-), not the Python interpreter; this repository contains playable images.
Electron/BBC puzzle game release media and play instructions with no recovered-source or developer-tool artifact.
Annotated BASIC and inline assembly SPEED.txt demonstrates and times Electron screen mode, keyboard and MOS speed techniques. Contains source; CLK limitations documented.
Native RISC OS telnet/terminal application source, historically relevant but this repository does not demonstrate recovered historic binary analysis or a specific reverse-engineering tool.
High-resolution PCB photographs of Acorn Risc PC hardware; no software reconstruction or development tool.
Parameterized OpenSCAD models for physical Risc PC case buttons/pins; hardware enclosure recreation, outside software scope.

A distinct playable C reimplementation based on the author’s prior snapshot-derived SkoolKit disassembly (great-escape-spectrum). CONVERSION.md describes translating annotated Z80 logic and data into C; README describes macOS/Windows/RISC OS builds and a Web port. “Runs exactly like the original” is a behavioral claim, not a byte-identical build of the original Spectrum binary.

Independent NESRecomp title project for Gumshoe; primary README documents title-specific static recompilation status and native x64 output.
Historical DOSBox/IDA debugger; project README.md explicitly moves to lab313ru/dsbxida. Preserve predecessor as reference and investigate successor separately.
PsyQ SDK LIB/OBJ signature corpus and generator consumed by the PSX loaders. Track as companion reference source rather than an additional loader project.
Fresh-search slice for PC Engine/HuC6280 disassembly and source reconstruction; three independent disassemblers were reviewed and promoted.
Fresh-search slice for classic Macintosh 68K disassembly and reconstruction; promoted resource_dasm and deduplicated the tracked Macintosh ROM reconstruction.
Fresh-search slice for Atari 8-bit source reconstruction and disassembly; promoted ardungeon and deduplicated the tracked Star Raiders reconstruction.

General-purpose Atari Jaguar graphics, palette and compressed-ROM analysis tool.

Byte-identical Alien Soldier Mega Drive reconstruction with binary tracing and emulator validation.

Fresh Atari Jaguar archaeology/tooling search; reviewed and promoted the restored SDK and jagfx.
Fresh Mega Drive source-reconstruction search; reviewed and promoted Flicky and Alien Soldier.

Authored Atari ST conversion of Dinamic Babaliba. README describes observing the Spectrum game and recreating graphics pixel by pixel, retaining map/mechanics and adding saves, pause and POKEs. C game, asset conversion scripts and TOS releases are published; no binary-derived reconstruction claim.

Source-derived native Doom port for low-memory 68000-family computers, based on FrenkelS/Doom8088. README documents Episode 1 only, reduced rendering and no music/saves/multiplayer; Atari ST backend and build script are published. This is a native source port, not reverse engineering.

Cross-compilation and remote-debug development system using GCC/newlib/binutils, a purpose-written TOS GDB server and ELF-to-PRG conversion that preserves symbol addresses. Source inventory includes packet/protocol, exception/context handling and converter implementation. The Windows build is documented as problematic; no host or hardware operation was independently reproduced.

Python compiler for an assembly-first high-level language with typed control flow, inline assembly, macros, register control and Amiga libraries. hasc contains parser, AST, validators, code generator and optimizer; asset tools and examples remain part of this coherent compiler project. The compiler emits assembly and requires separately installed vasm/vlink for executables.

Linux automation pipeline for Amiga assembly projects: GIMP/PNG/IFF conversion, ZX0 packing, copper palette/icon generation, assembly/linking and bootable ADF construction. Includes a credited demonstration derived from Bare-Metal Amiga Programming and Salvador decompression; catalogue scope is the integrated development tooling, not a new disassembly.

Integrated CPC development environment with bitmap/tile/sprite/map conversion, palette solving, RASM builds, scriptable exports and timing-validated Z80 raster-handler generation. README marks CPC/CPC+ supported while Spectrum, C64 and MSX are only prepared for; do not advertise those planned targets as implemented.

Original C64 puzzle shooter with substantial published PyCo game source, graphics/music includes and build configuration. README states its PyCo compiler remains private and generated assembly/PRG/D64 outputs are not in this repository; public reproducible compilation is therefore unverified, despite documented play controls and runtime instructions.

Released CPC 6128 fan conversion based on Master System OutRun. Michel Louvet states Claude Code wrote a native Z80 engine and extraction/music tools, with measured tracks, scenery and handling and SN76489-to-AY music conversion. Author reports emulator and real-hardware testing. Inspected Outrun V0.8.zip contains only Outrun V0.8.dsk (194816 bytes); no source or patches were linked, so source availability/compilability and detailed architecture remain unverified. Claims of native rewriting and AI model identity are attributed to the author, not independently reproduced.

Primary README and kernel/documentation inventory establish ongoing community maintenance of the existing open-source MiNT system. Keep as a reference/source node, rather than a new reconstruction or substantial newly authored port under the source-map rule that routine open-source maintenance alone is not an independent catalogue addition.

Primary README and src/DW6000.ino establish a Teensy-based hardware MIDI/SysEx editor. The CPC mention is autobiographical background, not published CPC software or recovery of the historical editor. Outside this legacy-computer development pass.

The cached upstream page documents a Rust CPC 6128 emulator with Z80 stepping, disassembly, breakpoints, watchpoints and traces. Current repository metadata and raw README fetches both return 404. Recheck the repository's public availability or locate its current canonical URL and inspect the core before promoting.

Repository is a third-party binary distribution collection: D64/PRG/TAP images, screenshots, descriptions and a game-list XML. It provides no source, disassembly, analysis or independent development tooling, so it is a discovery source rather than a standalone project.

Concrete TypeScript CLI provides C64 Ultimate program/media deployment, scripted machine control, PETSCII keyboard input, and implemented D64 directory parsing/creation/renaming. These are directly relevant retro-development and disk-image tools at coherent repository scope.

Synthesizable CPC system implementation extends Miguel Angel Rodriguez Jodar's CPC464 design with 128 KB banking and SD-backed two-drive disk emulation. The repository includes machine integration RTL, Z80 core, disk-controller logic, project files and known-good board releases; this is a general CPC implementation, not game-specific emulation.

Substantive C11 implementation of the C64 and 1541 as separate cycle-stepped machines, with disk handling, peripheral models, tests, snapshots and bus watchpoints. Documentation and source establish a general emulator useful for debugging historical software.

Author-published original C64 arcade game sources include substantial KickC game logic, level data, native assembly support and a documented build. Qualifies as concrete homebrew/native development under the current scope; no reverse-engineering provenance is claimed.

Substantial original Z80 game source, RASM build pipeline and ready-to-run CPC disk image demonstrate concrete native homebrew. The custom Z80 emulator/profiler is supporting testing infrastructure; the promoted output is a native CPC game.

Original C64 game implementation contains substantial native assembly, generated tile/sprite assets, a build/run script, and dated PRG snapshots. The author documents gameplay controls, completed tagged playthroughs and concrete raster/renderer optimization work.

Archive preserves programmer-supplied original game sources and disk artifacts and makes the tokenized Turbo Assembler source readable through documented extraction. This is source preservation under the broadened scope, not binary-derived reconstruction or a new disassembly.

Substantive native CPC C/inline-Z80 game code, localized disk/tape builds and assets establish original homebrew. The RVM web portal runs the native CPC output; it is ancillary and does not turn the repository into a game-specific-emulation-only project.

Original 1995 Citadel game source, data and editor archive, with substantive 68000 game-engine code and documented AsmOne build/run steps. Qualifies as original-source preservation under the broadened retro-development scope; it is not a binary-derived reconstruction.

Concrete C hardware-support/game framework for classic Amiga, including blitter/copper/input implementations, example showcase and asset-conversion tooling. This is original native retro-development infrastructure, not a game-specific emulator.

Substantive original 1990s Amiga assembly.library code is present in public/download/asm, including the library resident/function table and implementations, plus C interfaces and examples. The enclosing modern documentation site and archive form one project.

Restores and modernizes Menace code published across Amiga Format coverdisks, with assembled-game documentation and substantive updated source. Includes a C# decoder for the game's graphics data; this is more than a passive magazine mirror.

Active continuation of the historical ACE BASIC compiler with real K&R C parser/code-generator source, 68k runtime libraries, modern VBCC build migration and test tooling. The native compiler and IDE support form a single coherent development project.

Despite the Hello World title, the repository implements a replacement icon.library for booting ROM Workbench, a dynamic version.library, OFS image/bootblock tools and compatibility research. These are concrete system reimplementation and retro-development artifacts.

Early-stage native Amiga C framework with actual runtime/rendering/input/sound implementations, game showcases, asset conversion and a distributed VS Code extension. Repository-wide scope covers the framework and its companion tools.

Distinct native Atari ST C/assembly port descended from released Sopwith/SDL Sopwith source, with a real Atari framebuffer/blitter backend and downloadable .TOS/.ST releases. Upstream fork status does not make it a passive duplicate.

Primarily republishes perihelion's existing Atari ST tutorials as AsciiDoc and separates/reformats their assembly examples, with only minor edits. Its short Makefile orchestrates existing vasm, zip2st and Hatari. Reviewed source establishes an educational reference rather than a distinct recovered program or independently implemented development/recovery tool, so retain a source/decision but no separate project.

One original homebrew card game with shared C game rules and platform-specific native backends across vintage machines, including concrete Amiga and Atari ST implementations and upstream gameplay verification. Track the coherent whole repository rather than splitting each port.

Substantial restoration and continued development of the original DICE compiler suite, with an implemented 68k code generator, native assembly helpers, assembler, linker and runtime source. Qualifies as historical development-tool preservation and directly relevant native toolchain work.

Creator-published, substantial native 68000 Amiga intro implementation with multiple effects, hardware takeover/restore, music integration and assembly instructions. Track the complete intro rather than separate effect files.
Substantial native fan conversion with first-person development notes, translated C++ game logic and Amiga-specific assembly/rendering. Source translation, not embedded guest-CPU emulation.

Creator-published recovery of substantial original 1988 Amiga game code plus concrete source-based native Python/JavaScript recreations. The modern paths implement game logic directly and do not use game-specific CPU pseudo-emulation.
Substantial creator-attributed native Amiga homebrew/spin-off implementation, corroborated by the creator's released-game page. Actual game source extends far beyond a copied loader/template.

Substantive original Atari ST game source and assets, with author/date headers and concrete 68k game/polygon implementation. Historical preservation qualifies independently of unknown buildability; not labelled a binary-derived disassembly.

Concrete historical game-source restoration with substantial game logic and modified C build scaffolding. Actual x86/DOS code overrides the misleading ST repository label. Missing runtime stubs limit completeness but do not negate the existing archival/restoration work.

Substantial period programming environment with preserved Atari ST/Unix source, interpreter, editor, debugger and actual portability scaffolding. Qualifies as historical development-tool preservation, not a tutorial or unrelated modern application.

Concrete binary-derived patch implementations, identified game offsets and documented compatibility defects. A small README is unnecessary: source comments and substantive assembly establish the work. Track the coherent patch collection at repository scope.

Preserves the original 1986 FujiBoink C/68000 demo source and period documentation. The already tracked mnemo70/fujiboink conversion repository retains the same six historical ST source components under st_source, with matching creator/date headers and implementation. Retain this useful original-source reference linked to that lineage, without adding a second overlapping source-only project.

Substantial annotated Ghost Town recovery includes original-platform logic, bug fixes, languages, graphics, SID music and native C64/C128 conversion. The two ports and supporting tools are one coherent repository-wide project.

Five source listings contain concrete C64 intro disassembly with origin links, labels and analysis of raster interrupts, scrolling, system calls and music. Lack of a README/build script does not negate the existing research; catalogue at whole-repository scope.

Concrete labelled disassembly and sequencer/pattern analysis of C64 International Karate SID and multiple Atari POKEY players, accompanied by Frida projects and source music files. This is subsystem research rather than full-game reconstruction and is kept as one coherent archive.

Implemented Ruby library provides VIC-II image conversion, 6502 assembly/byte generation, PRG merging, VICE snapshot injection and ca65/ld65/Exomizer build automation. It is directly relevant development tooling beyond its short library overview.

Concrete Java/Swing cross-development tool converts images to C64 multicolor data and exports Koala files, with palette selection, per-cell color constraints, dithering and a GUI. The nested NetBeans project is the repository's single tool.

Working implementation exists for project-aware Oscar64 compile commands, asynchronous process handling, Quickfix compiler diagnostics, assembly viewing and VICE/RetroDebugger launch. This is a distinct Neovim integration, not an independent compiler/emulator.

Creator-published Scorpion source contains substantial Mutant Monty game logic, actors, 41 level maps, graphics and sound, with released Amiga ADF/WHDLoad builds linked from the creator page. It qualifies as a native fan conversion; original C64/CPC binary analysis is not claimed.

Creator documents recovery of his unfinished 1985 C64 Moon Patrol conversion by disassembling and reassembling the old binary in 2024, then implementing substantial missing gameplay. Published PRG/D64 outputs and explicit PAL VICE play testing support a concrete restoration even though recovered source files are not published.

Michael Buhidar republishes and verifies his own 1983/84 C64 BASIC game from the October 1984 Ahoy! type-in. Complete game listing and tokenized PRG are present, with original-author provenance, line-check verification and explicit VICE operation.

README identifies this as a converter of mist64/c64disasm's existing hex-assembly text into BASIC/KERNAL binary images. c64_read_dis.erl parses listed addresses/bytes, fills address gaps and writes bytes; it adds no independent disassembly, recovery analysis or substantive compiler. Excluded under the workflow's rule for merely converting somebody else's analysis; original listing attribution is preserved.

RAM-derived CPC Knight Lore reconstruction contains symbolic Z80 assembly, data extraction and detailed engine analysis, with original and experimental rendering branches. Primary main-branch documentation reports successful RASM assembly and standalone snapshot boot to the real menu. This does not establish full playability or complete byte matching; the browser component is described only as a room visualizer.

Substantive Kotlin/LibGDX recreation of Fruity Frank with game-state, enemies, collision, scoring and desktop/Android launchers. It recreates CPC gameplay rather than documenting binary-derived reconstruction. Gradle pins old Kotlin/Android dependencies; no independent build or run was performed.

Author-published 2018 CPC remake of the Dinamic game, with substantial native assembly, room data, audio and public English/Spanish CDT plus DSK releases. No binary-derived reconstruction or byte-equivalence claim is made.

Original C#/MonoGame re-creation of the CPC Airwolf gameplay with real level, enemy, helicopter, collision and UI code. Creator explicitly says it is not emulation, recreates only gameplay and may omit original features. This is a modern remake, not a native CPC port or a claimed disassembly.

Substantive CPC C/assembly development framework, low-level hardware library, asset tools and reproducible-project build infrastructure. Inspected keyboard implementation directly programs the PPI/PSG; examples and content tools form the same coherent repository.

Author-maintained C Z80 cross-assembler includes CPC cartridge/snapshot/disk/tape generation, integrated compression, patching support and debug symbols. Inspected actual assembler source, integrated API example and build files. Z80 is the output instruction set, not a claim that the host executable runs on Z80.

Original author preserved and annotated the commercial 1985 CPC DAMS source, with a tokenized-source encoder/decoder and documented self-hosting rebuild procedure. Actual dams.dams assembly and C++ conversion tool establish substantive source restoration, not a binary-only distribution.

Concrete fast CPC tape loader with adaptive pulse measurement, synchronization and native loading code, paired with a Python CDT generator. Source credits Mert Boru's TurboLoader as the basis; this repository adds an implemented paired workflow rather than a passive binary mirror.

Author-maintained native diagnostic suite tests RAM, ROM, keyboard and CRTC behavior, with substantial hardware routines and distinct ROM, RAM, cartridge, disk and tape build variants. Companion ROM dump code supports retro system investigation.

Creator-published multi-platform native adventure game source, with substantial CPC/C64 C game code and Amiga assembly implementation plus asset/build tools. Track the common game once at repository scope; referenced Spectrum/ST ports are not claimed as present in this repository.
README and source establish a playable experimental C++/SDL port translated from Richard Dymond's SkoolKit Z80 disassembly while retaining the original memory-address model.
Recovered Rebelstar Raiders Sinclair BASIC and Z80 source extracted from original TZX media with documented Go/Python tooling and added annotations.
Host-side Go converter for ZX Spectrum SCR screen data with documented PNG/GIF/JPEG output, scaling and border handling.
Fully documented ZX Spectrum Z80 disassembly with named routines, classified data and a byte-exact SjASM+/M8XXX rebuild comparison.
ZX Spectrum Eric & the Floaters Z80 disassembly with SjASM+ build source and extracted code/data organization.
CPCSDK command-line DSK editor that manipulates files and AMSDOS headers and lists tokenized BASIC and DAMS source.
Cross-platform CPC/CPC+ emulator with a debugger, headless execution, JSON control server, hardware-state inspection and source-level DAP integration.
Reproducible Atari ST cross-development container bundling 68000 assembly/C toolchains, libraries, AGT and automation helpers.
Fresh CPC homebrew/source route; reviewed and promoted iDSK and SugarboxV2 from relevant results while discarding unrelated matches.
Fresh Archimedes disassembly route; reviewed top results resolved to already indexed Mark Moxon projects, including the previously recorded Lander duplicate.
Fresh SG-1000/SC-3000 disassembly route; the reviewed leading project was the already indexed Gearsystem emulator/debugger and its existing duplicate decision was retained.

Primary repository for the TRS-80/TCS Genie IIIs emulator and controller archaeology work.

Primary repository for the multi-platform ROM development and analysis environment.

Sega Saturn emulator reviewed from the Saturn search; upstream explicitly says it is game-first and not a game-development tool.
Apple II/IIgs cycle-oriented browser emulator with built-in debugger, disk explorer, disassembler and agent-control interfaces.
Profile revisited: two complete byte-exact MSX reassemblies promoted; ordinary emulator ports recorded as exclusions.
Annotated Z80 disassembly of the MSX1 Booga-Boo release with a documented hash-checked build.
Clean-room Zanac AI research plus a full MSX Z80 disassembly, structured knowledge base and Claude-operated sprint workflow.
Playable browser reimplementation derived routine-by-routine from the MSX2 Metal Gear disassembly, with explicit coverage and headless tests.
MSX search lead whose repository content was unavailable during review; retained only for a future identity check.
Primary repository for Oric Explorer, an Oric media browser with 6502 disassembly, filesystem and graphics inspection.
Git mirror of the official Oric Software Development Kit, reviewed as one toolchain project rather than a separate mirror-derived work.
Primary source repository for José María Enguita's original Blake's 7 fan adventure for Oric hardware.
Current Atari Lynx emulator/debugger with source-level debugging, broad symbol support and an embedded MCP server.
Primary repository for a clean Atari Lynx port that executes the original NES Super Mario Bros. game logic through a hardware adapter layer.
Primary source for an original Atari Lynx music tracker with verified hardware builds, sample tooling and ComLynx/MIDI bridges.
Primary Ultima V decompilation with assembly-level semantic matching and playable modern/DOS targets.
Primary successor to restunts with Ghidra-exported assembly, reproducible DOS reconstruction and cross-platform verification tests.

DOS EGA/CGA/Hercules and separately reconstructed Amiga versions share a coherent SDL3 port repository. Real-mode or 68000 memory layouts are retained as data, while gameplay is native C. Original EXE/ADF assets remain required.
Reconstructs the DOS EGA Collection version with Supercars/Muscle Cars and California/European scenery. CGA/Hercules and Tandy paths remain unported; original data files are required.

Native C reconstruction of the VGA version, all five cars and both courses, with AdLib/Sound Blaster and PC-speaker output. EGA/Tandy graphics and several sound devices are not ported; original game data is required.

Native C reconstruction of the full VGA game with optional Street Rod SE car data. Maintains original data/memory structure, adds a launcher, and requires original assets; alternate graphics adapters remain unported.

Native C reconstruction of INTRO.EXE, PS.EXE and AP.EXE in one process, based on CD version 1.2. VGA/AdLib gameplay is reported working; other sound devices and reported carrier-deck rendering issues remain. Original executable/data resources are required.

Ports CityAceE's documented Z80 Batty disassembly into native 386 protected-mode DOS C++. Upstream reports all 15 levels and all three modes playable plus pixel/frame parity gates. Those bounded parity checks do not establish a byte-identical original Spectrum binary.

Reconstructs DOS Micro Machines gameplay, asset formats, sound and track editing in browser JavaScript. Author describes a playable one-player tournament and partially complete two-human modes; repository source and evidence distinguish proven, static and unresolved behavior. Original game files are loaded locally.

Evidence-grounded DOS GODS reconstruction with decoded formats, browser renderer, movement/combat and level editor. Native JS source is inspected; the README preserves open enemy-strategy, level-sequencing and other fidelity gaps. Track as partial reconstruction, not a verified complete game. Historical Gods/gods-web work is merged into this root repository.

Annotated reconstruction of Tim Clarke's Mars voxel demo and an independent JavaScript renderer. A separate purpose-built x86 emulator is the differential oracle, not the browser render path. Author-reported pixel equality across selected seeds is image parity, not original-binary byte exactness. Actual browser source is now in site/mars.js, despite stale web/ paths in some README sections.
Primary README explicitly retires this DOS_RE 1.0 starter in favor of the already tracked dos_re 2.0 repository; preserve the predecessor identity without duplicating that recovery-framework lineage.

Primary README explicitly says no reversing run has started and no gameplay fidelity is established. The current repository is experiment preparation, bundled third-party inputs and adapted tool configuration, without demonstrated game reconstruction; re-review if actual independently authored recovered implementation appears.

The reviewed root is the Soggy-1000 hardware clone/KiCad project. Its software/ramtest is acknowledged as a small board-specific RAM and paging bring-up program, but the hardware root is not promoted as an independent historical-software reconstruction or general development suite.

Explicitly requested candidate; native 68030/68060 port with substantial Amiga-specific implementation, build targets and author-reported full gameplay.

Generic ST-family system emulator using Moira; no game-specific execution-path classification applies. Partly descended from the author's late-1990s emulator and Hatari; Moira provides the CPU core and Munt the MT-32 synthesis. Kept as one generic emulator root.

Native decompression library, host packers and music-data tooling; ZX1/YM data formats are not source platforms. Based on Einar Saukas's ZX1 format/algorithm; repository contains ST1, jx1, nx1 and YX6 as one coherent toolkit. Related ST4 references do not add a candidate.

Original native demo, not reconstructed historical program code; work_kinds intentionally empty. MegaBuSTers demo with its own source and package root. Included YM register dump avoids redistributing the restricted original SNDH player. License has additional AGPL terms.

Original C/68k homebrew demo and development example, not an RE-derived port. Separate demo root using the atarist-toolkit-docker environment and libcmini. Emulator recommendations do not add emulator-host output platforms.

Generic Macintosh system emulator port running natively on AmigaOS, not a native Macintosh application port or game-specific wrapper. Port of Mini vMac 36.04 pinned to ryandesign/minivmac revision cee5685e76d3953cfdfcc83b937b13d7de2383f8; Mac Plus and two Mac II variants plus HFS bridge stay at root scope.

Source-based native application port with Amiga DOS/process/socket glue; no ixemul and no CPU-emulated application execution. Derivative of pgul/binkd retained as the independent Amiga native-port root. Old concurrency comments in Makefile are not used to override the current implementation/release history.

Restoration and continued development of published historical browser source, not binary decompilation. Independent of Yvon Rozijn and the former AWeb team; based on 2003 AWeb 3.4 with selected 3.5 integration. OS4 execution is the 68k binary, not a native PowerPC output.

Historical Amiga Python preservation/revival and language runtime. Python version numbers are subjects, not platform labels. Irmen de Jong's 1999–2000 Amiga port is preserved by the independent amigazen project; README expressly disclaims lineage with OS4 Python.

Restoration/extension of historical Amiga Unix-library and utility ports plus new shell/runtime work, retained as one coherent environment. UniLib3 descends from David Gay's unix.lib with Enrico Forestieri and Irmen de Jong contributions; component origins/licenses differ. All included components stay at repository scope.

Original-source preservation of a multitasking GEM AES replacement, not decompiled source. Official Gribnif Software source publication; distinct from NeoDesk, the same publisher's desktop application.

Historical replacement-desktop source preservation rather than reverse-engineered recovery. Official Gribnif Software NeoDesk source root, distinct from Geneva's AES replacement. Internal executables are not split into duplicate projects.

Original native homebrew/historical revival; not evidence of binary reverse engineering. Source platform/CPU and RE work fields stay empty. Game root is separate from reusable toybox dependency; host blitter emulation is a development aid and does not make the Atari executable CPU-emulated.

Original SDL homebrew game with portable/native targets; not a reconstructed historical binary. One original game root with desktop and handheld ports. Platform subdirectories are not independent project identities.

Music-data packing and native playback tooling; YM2149 register streams are data, not a historical source platform. LZSA-like compression toolkit with its own packer and native player; distinct from maxYMiser. Single repository scope retained.

Restoration/maintenance of a published native development-tool port; not a binary-derived port. Independent amigazen revival of GNU Make 4.4.1 via dmcoles/gnu_make_amiga; distinct from GNU upstream and companion ToolKit. No separate predecessor promoted in this fragment.

Anthony Beaucamp’s original cross-development SDK combines CC65 target drivers, game projects and a script-generating builder. The C64 VIC-II driver directly configures target hardware. README lists the 6502-based output families and Windows/Linux builder workflows; these host environments are not claims of native Windows/Linux game ports.

The original coder recovered the source of a collaborative Forum-64 puzzle game initiated around 2005. Its cc65 C/assembly implementation and Makefile are substantial native C64 source. This is author-released homebrew source, not a disassembly of a commercial game.

Ricardo Quesada’s original native game implements Road Race, Cyclo Cross and Cross Country, with single-player and face-to-face controls. Upstream v0.4 documentation supplies a D64 download, gameplay instructions and a video while explicitly saying the game is unfinished.

Jason Kelk’s original source credits him for code, graphics and sound effects. The ACME assembly contains native C64 memory layout, seven level indices, sprite construction and character display code; a PRG is also committed.

Original EXTERN extension for DAAD adventure interpreters, providing access to disks, SD cards, cartridges and related storage/display functions. Separate native target modules include C64/Plus/4, CPC, Spectrum-family, MSX and PCW implementations. The Amiga source explicitly says WORK IN PROGRESS, NOT COMPLETED. Repository-description MSDOS support was not established from the inspected source tree and is omitted.

Competition-hosted source release of Toni Ramírez’s original 2015 game, with C gameplay, CPCtelera hardware/audio calls and assets. Upstream calls it the CPCRetroDev 2015 winner; that placement is an attributed upstream claim.

César Nicolás González/CNGSoft’s original CPC game is released through the competition source archive. Substantial FROGALOT.S80 code and include data implement CPC startup, display and gameplay. README attributes second place and a technical-achievement award to the 2015 contest.

Rantan Games’ David Girón Jareño and Sandra María Garzón Hernández released this original CPC game through the CPCRetroDev source archive. Native C gameplay, heroes, maps, sprites and audio are present. Third place in the 2015 contest is reported by upstream.

Shinra’s Adrien Destugues and Cédric Quetier provide an original native CPC implementation of the credited ZNAX concept/rules. Code covers gameplay, scoring, keyboard and CPC hardware. The repository reports fifth place at CPCRetroDev 2015 and includes older development history.

Original September 2015 CPC game by the cpc-power.com team, released as BASIC listings, Z80 components and explanatory source notes. Upstream reports fourth place in CPCRetroDev 2015 and credits Bruno Kukulcan, Tom & Jerry/GPA, CED and testers.

Fresh root and substantive canonical native macOS emulator, but tracked vAmigaNet/vAmigaNet and vAmigaDOS/vAmigaDOS already share its core. MIT-licensed C++20 Rigid Disk Block/partition reader is real source, but upstream explicitly calls it a debugger-driven code example. CMake downloads an unpinned AROS hardblocks.h at configure time. Windows/Mac examples are suggested uses; Linux-oriented netinet/in.h code is present and no Windows build was verified. The Amiga RDB data format does not establish a m68k CPU for this host tool.

TOSEMU is Johan Toverland Thelin’s hosted environment for original Atari TOS executables, not a decompilation of one guest application. The current PRG loader opens and maps the supplied file, checks magic 0x601A, constructs the guest environment and applies relocation entries. The tosemu executable runs a program directly; the separate tosaesd daemon supports shared GEM accessory sessions and is not a prerequisite for a single CLI invocation. README explicitly targets integration into Linux and excludes general games/demos. This repository is counted once; its hosted EmuTOS and Musashi components are dependencies, not additional runner discoveries. Canonical repository and lineage aliases were screened against the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and prior dedup index; no existing counted project matched. Source snapshot 443340b2dfcf9e691a080bc4e3722102bc9c2839, non-truncated tree with 274 entries. Tooling: original-binary CPU emulation plus TOS system-call reimplementation. src/musashi.c intercepts traps 1, 2, 13 and 14 for GEMDOS, GEM, BIOS and XBIOS, while src/gemdosfile.c maps guest file reads to host stdio and copies data into emulated memory. The guest instructions still execute in Musashi; native host API handling does not make the guest a source port or ahead-of-time translation. Hosted EmuTOS AES/VDI routines supply graphical APIs without booting an Atari ROM. Terminal usage, headless support and self-hosted retro development tests establish the requested runner category, without implying complete TOS or ST hardware compatibility. README describes inspiration from 68kemu and Wine; neither is merged into this project identity. .gitmodules pins separate Musashi and EmuTOS dependencies; the inspected gitlinks are Musashi 313ebf1bd9f4d0d93341eb5ce21fd8a119e9dbdd and EmuTOS 978e37569bff95841e42675d11fcc6799aad8483. TOSEMU’s COPYING carries GPLv2 and source headers allow v2 or later; Musashi has its permissive MIT-like grant, and the hosted EmuTOS documentation records its GPL lineage. README/Makefile explicitly distinguish bundled later-CPU SoftFloat/MAME code from what upstream says is linked, so redistribution still needs the actual chosen build/dependency licenses checked. Original HiSoft Devpac 3.10 GEN.TTP and Lattice C 5.60 LC1.TTP, LC2.TTP, CLINK.TTP, LC.TTP and MAKE.TTP have documented upstream test recipes; those commercial installations must be obtained separately under their own rights. Their upstream self-hosting/byte-comparison claims are not independent verification by this audit. Broader author, dependency and historical-host graph coverage remains partial. ParaTos is an experimental direct runner for original Atari TOS/MiNT command-line applications. README identifies Linux and explains the system-call translation approach. gemdos/loader.c reads and endian-converts the PRG header, builds the basepage/environment, copies text/data, applies relocation fixups and appends ARGV data. paratos.c loads the named executable and enters the CPU engine directly, without an ST machine boot. A 2023 upstream commit explicitly added OSX support, and current Apple-specific executable-path and byte-order code remains present; this refines the earlier discovery’s Linux-only evidence without asserting that a modern macOS build was tested. Canonical repository and lineage aliases were screened against the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and prior dedup index; no existing counted project matched. Source snapshot 9d43e70bce3ed4f82ee43e35375994332fc2ac4b, non-truncated tree with 106 entries. Tooling with CPU-emulator and GEMDOS/API-reimplementation capabilities. ParaTos invokes Musashi to execute original 68k instructions and dispatches guest trap calls to native host implementations; gemdos/path.c converts TOS/MiNT filenames to POSIX paths, with case-insensitive and 8.3-name lookup. It accepts U: and rejects other drive-letter mappings in this snapshot. This is not a compiler translating the guest to host source and not an ST hardware emulator. README restricts the intended programs to clean command-line tools avoiding direct hardware and OS trap-vector patching. The implementation is incomplete, and minimal BIOS/AES/VDI paths do not establish a desktop compatibility environment. README explicitly credits Vincent Riviere’s 68kemu as inspiration; that relation is not a same-project alias or proof of shared source. The bundled mushashi directory supplies Musashi CPU code under its MIT-like grant. ParaTos COPYING contains GPLv3; README also identifies GPL-licensed TOS syscall documentation taken from the Atari Compendium/TOSHYP site. Original guest programs retain their own licenses; the runner’s license does not authorize redistribution of commercial tools. The repository provides source for small cross-compiled syscall tests, but no primary source checked here establishes that an original commercial compiler runs. The OSX-support and macOS alignment commits show deliberate host-port work, while current usability and broader binary compatibility remain untested. Broader author, dependency and historical-host graph coverage remains partial. Tooling: original ARM instruction execution combined with RISC OS SWI/SharedCLib reimplementation, focused on command-line software rather than a whole Archimedes machine. configure.ac selects ARMulator by default, sleeve as an alternate interpreter, or a separate native ARM backend. src/swi.c dispatches registered native handlers, and xosfile_load_stamped translates a RISC OS filename then uses host open/fstat/read. Runtime API coverage is partial, and unregistered SWIs return an error in the inspected tip. The SourceForge site, repo.or.cz location and hamishcoleman GitHub copy are recorded as a single riscose lineage, not three discoveries. The current tree incorporates ARMulator, sleeve, OSLib-derived SWI definitions and native compatibility handlers; none is independently promoted in this fragment. The original author states a GNU GPL distribution license, ARMulator armemu.c specifically carries GPLv2-or-later, and mod/LICENSE contains Apache-2.0 text for that directory’s separate material. The tree has no repository-root license file in the inspected listing, so dependency/module licensing must not be flattened into a claim that every bundled file has identical terms. The author’s 2001 diary reports Norcroft cc plus Acorn’s linker building and running Hello World, which is historical upstream evidence only. The separate test-input listing includes grep, unzip and zipinfo, explicitly excludes distribution of Norcroft cc, and does not establish complete correctness. Contributor Ralph Corderoy’s primary account also reports the Twin CLI text editor running; that historical report is retained without claiming a current reproduced test. Old TODO/PROBLEMS note SharedCLib FILE-layout and UnixLib/OS_CLI gaps; their exact present status is unresolved. Broader author, dependency and historical-host graph coverage remains partial. Substantive emulator/development tooling: src/linker.rs builds transition-vector shims for imported symbols; src/emulator/mod.rs installs InterfaceLib/StdCLib and Toolbox/C-library callbacks and handles them through a PowerPC supervisor-call hook. Original PEF instructions run inside Unicorn without booting Classic Mac OS. Missing imports remain logged, the initialization vector is explicitly unimplemented, and the README lists missing PEF relocations and APIs. XCOFF support is not established. Cargo.toml selects Rust edition 2021, unicorn-engine dependency version range 2.0.1 and xattr 0.2.2 among the parser/runtime dependencies. No host build recipe matrix or CI exists in the complete tree. PR #1 reports Linux DeRez working only after manually commenting out the xattr::SUPPORTED_PLATFORM branch; that branch still exists at the reviewed tip and the same report reaches unimplemented fseek. Source availability and dependency declarations do not establish a clean build on all intended hosts. All four build flags remain null; no candidate compilation, guest execution, emulation, gameplay or byte comparison was performed. The complete 37-entry tree has no LICENSE/COPYING grant, Cargo.toml has no license field, and repository metadata reports license null. Do not describe it as permissively licensed or assume public source authorizes redistribution. Unicorn and Rust dependencies retain their separate terms, as do original CodeWarrior/MPW executables and libraries. README’s comparison with SheepShaver/QEMU describes the purpose; no fork relationship is established. Merged PR #1 concerns Retro68-produced MacBinary II input and is not evidence that Retro68 is this runner’s implementation or guest CPU. Warren Toomey’s Apout loads original PDP-11 Unix a.out programs, interprets user-mode instructions and maps TRAP system calls to native Unix calls without booting a guest OS or disk filesystem. Current README 2.4 reports testing on 64-bit Debian Linux. Emulator/development tooling: cpu.c fetches and dispatches original PDP-11 instructions, while v7trap.c directly implements guest read/write/open through native calls and bsdtrap.c provides a separate 2.11BSD ABI. APOUT_ROOT rewrites absolute guest paths; relative paths remain host-relative. This is not a full PDP-11 machine or guest OS boot. It provides host-file access, not containment; NATIVES is enabled by the Makefile and unrecognized binaries can be attempted with host execv. The Makefile builds C sources with a C compiler, make and libm, with configurable emulation/debug options. Its current default APOUT_OPTIONS uses -DEMU211 -DEMUv1 -DNATIVES, but source checks the uppercase EMUV1; consequently the default spelling does not enable V1/V2. README likewise says V1 is disabled by default. README 2.4 is current but the Makefile’s distribution VERSION remains apout2.3beta1, so that old packaging string is not the current release claim. The nested 68000 build uses m68k-elf-gcc, explicit 68000 options and newlib BSP support. NT Virtual CP/M Machine is a standalone C++ command-line runner for CP/M .COM tools. ntvcm.cxx loads a selected host file at guest 0x100, creates CP/M entry hooks and enters x80.cxx. README documents asm/load, Turbo Pascal, Aztec C, WordStar and many other tools; they are compatibility examples, not separately reconstructed projects. The current head has removed the former GDB/MI debugger-host mode, so it is not advertised as a current capability. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: be598f65c1b649f5250dcd6d8fef266b1b86413e. An emulator with native CP/M BDOS/file and console translation, an 8080/Z80 trace disassembler and optional per-PC CSV profiling. The loader creates PSP/environment and synthetic interrupt stubs; DOS file calls use native host fopen/fread/fwrite and -r maps a host directory to C:. Original executables run without a booted DOS OS or vendor ROM in the normal path. Optional boot-sector loading does not establish a complete PC hardware emulator. MSVC/g++ scripts build the C++ interpreter/runtime; Linux release links statically with OpenMP and macOS uses pthread/signed-char settings. mr.sh deliberately uses -O2 and documents a maintainer-observed g++11.4 -O3/-Ofast code-generation problem. The original C engine has graphics, animation, actors, inventory, dialogues, bytecode execution and audio; the modern code has game state, navigation, scripts, scenes, menus and sound. inga-sdl is the canonical tracked root; inga-amigaos3 is an original-engine source alias, not a second project. Original Inga/Ermentrud history and the modern SDL engine are consolidated as one lineage, including the separate inga-amigaos3 repository and any legacy copies in the modern tree. The separately hosted original root has no top-level LICENSE; do not silently extend the modern license to every original file or to Ermentrud artwork/story/audio. The author's game page lists separate released packages. SDL2 and its component libraries are dependencies, not additional game discoveries. Broader history, asset and port-package provenance remain partial. Broader author, dependency and source graph coverage is partial. Darren Banfi’s AmIga Minesweeper is a distinct original native Amiga implementation, with source, screenshot and author README rather than an emulator wrapper or a mirror of another Minesweeper source release. The full minesweeper.c defines a 10-by-10 board with ten mines, adjacency counts, a queue-based empty-area reveal, flagging, mouse events, reset, win/loss handling and Amiga Intuition graphics/audio effects. It is not the same code lineage as Paul Kienitz’s Miner, despite sharing the game genre. The author’s root and title were absent from the current 1715 catalogue, source and decision indexes and 2031 prior-root union. Root LICENSE is MIT, copyright Darren Banfi 2024, and the C file names the same author. No external game-data download or commercial original binary is required by the documented code path. This distinct code is not merged with other Minesweeper homebrew merely because the rules match. The README clone command spells a different repository name; the verified canonical root is boingball/AmIgaMinesweeper and no unverified alternate URL is created. The OS compatibility contradiction is preserved for future validation rather than repaired during catalogue publication.

The embedded picture source and background image are game assets, but no blanket asset-rights grant was found. Report this licensing gap separately from the project’s eligibility as a substantive source-available game.
